title: Go: Testing Framework
description: Build a testing framework with assertion helpers, mocking, test suites, and table-driven test support.

steps.title: Assertion functions
steps.description: Define an `Assert` struct holding `*testing.T`. Implement `Equal(actual, expected interface{})`, `NotNil(val interface{})`, and `Error(err error)`. Each prints pass/fail to stdout. Test with `Equal(2+2, 4)` and print `"2+2=4"` on success.
hints: Call `t.Errorf` on failure, print `fmt.Printf("PASS: %s\n", msg)` on success.
Store a `msg string` field or pass messages explicitly.

verification.failureMessage: Equal should compare values and print PASS on match.

steps.title: Mock struct with Call and Return
steps.description: Design a `Mock` struct that records expected calls. Method `On(method string, args ...interface{}) *MockCall` sets up an expectation. `Return(ret ...interface{})` on `MockCall` registers the return values. `AssertExpectations(t *testing.T)` verifies all calls were made. Print the result of a mocked `Add(1, 2)` returning `3`.
hints: Store expectations in `[]*MockCall` with method name, args, and return values.
Track `called bool` on MockCall to verify expectations.

verification.successMessage: Mock records and returns expected values.
verification.failureMessage: MockCall should register return values and verify calls.

steps.title: Test suite with Setup/Teardown
steps.description: Create a `Suite` interface: `SetupTest()`, `TeardownTest()`. Build a `RunSuite(t *testing.T, suite Suite)` runner that calls SetupTest before each test method and TeardownTest after. Print `"setup"`, `"test body"`, and `"teardown"` to demonstrate lifecycle.
hints: Use `reflect` to find methods on the suite matching `TestXXX(*testing.T)` signatures.
Wrap each test call with `suite.SetupTest()` before and `suite.TeardownTest()` after.

verification.failureMessage: SetupTest must run before the test, TeardownTest after.

steps.title: Table-driven test helpers
steps.description: Implement `RunTable(t *testing.T, name string, cases []TestCase, fn func(t *testing.T, tc TestCase))`. `TestCase` has `Name string`, `Input interface{}`, and `Expected interface{}`. Each case runs as a sub-test. Print the name and result of each case.
hints: `TestCase` is a struct with Name, Input, Expected.
The `fn` callback receives `tc` and should call your assertion helpers.

verification.failureMessage: Each case should run as a named sub-test with assertions.

steps.title: Coverage tracker
steps.description: Build a `CoverageTracker` that records which lines or functions were executed. Use `Coverage()` and `Report()`. Mock a function that tracks calls. After running tests, print the coverage report with `fmt.Println(tracker.Report())`.
hints: Increment the counter in each tracked function.
`Report()` returns a formatted string like `"foo.go:10 -> 3 calls"`.

verification.failureMessage: Report should show function/file with execution count.
